subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Horsepower vs. Torque
description: A micro-lesson that makes Horsepower vs. Torque usable.

hook.text: Car ads brag about horsepower, but torque is what actually pushes you back in your seat.

buildup.text: Torque is rotational force—how hard the engine twists the crankshaft at any given moment.

discovery.text: Horsepower combines torque with speed. More horsepower means more work done faster.

twist.text: A diesel truck has massive torque but modest horsepower. A race car has both at high RPM.

climax.text: Torque gets you moving. Horsepower keeps you fast. You need both for a great driving experience.

punchline.text: Torque wins the sprint. Horsepower wins the race.

details.summary: Horsepower measures how fast an engine can do work over time, while torque measures the rotational force at the crankshaft. Together they define a vehicle's acceleration and top speed.
details.whyItMatters: Torque determines how quickly a car launches from a stop, while horsepower governs top speed. Understanding both helps drivers choose vehicles suited to their driving needs.
takeaways: Torque is rotational force measured in pound-feet or newton-meters
Horsepower equals torque multiplied by RPM divided by 5252
Diesel engines have high torque; gasoline engines often have high HP

faq.question: Why do electric motors feel so much faster off the line?
faq.answer: Electric motors deliver maximum torque instantly from zero RPM. Combustion engines must rev up to reach peak torque, creating a delay that makes them feel slower despite similar power ratings.

faq.question: Is more horsepower always better?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. A heavy truck with 300 horsepower but massive torque will tow better than a light sports car with 400 horsepower but less torque. The right balance depends on the vehicle's purpose.
